subject: Re: MAP & procurement delay — proposed staggered canary and rebaseline
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@biocrest.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@biocrest.com, tom.hayes@biocrest.com
Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP update — procurement window slipping

Hi Markus / Laura,

Quick update from our side: procurement has pushed our internal review to the week beginning 6/8 due to an unexpected budget committee backlog. That means signature timing is likely to slide out at least 2–3 weeks from the MAP target.

We still want to keep forward momentum on the evaluation plan (technical canary + performance eval), but we need a clearer contingency if sign-off misses the current close date. I've attached the latest SOW (v3) showing the scope we expect to go live on day one.

Can you share what a minimal canary would look like (scope + acceptance criteria) if we aim to decouple the canary from full contract signature? Also — any commercial levers for an interim arrangement while procurement finishes their work?

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Head of Clinical Ops, Biocrest Health
Attachment: Biocrest_SOW_v3.pdf
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@biocrest.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-18T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP update — procurement window slipping

Emily — thanks for the heads up and for the SOW. We can definitely design a staggered approach so your evaluation team can run a canary against a scoped set of features while procurement completes the legal/commercial sign-off.

High-level:
- Minimal canary (A): model inference + telemetry only; limit to 2 internal services, TTL=24h, max 10k tokens/day. Acceptance: 99th percentile latency under 220ms; embedding stability within 2% drift on test set.
- Expanded canary (B): add production routing and KV-cache persist; acceptance: successful end-to-end runbook and billing counter agree.

Commercially we can offer a 30-day interim trial with usage capped and a temporary MPA (mutual pilot agreement) that defers full billing until signature. If procurement prefers, we can instead issue a firm credit on first-month usage tied to execution of the SOW.

Risks I want logged now: procurement slip >3 weeks threatens the June release window; resource reservations (dedicated capacity) may need a short-term hold; exec alignment may be required if we need to extend our reserved pool.

Laura / Ben — please see risk bullets and confirm if ops/legal can issue a short MPA and an interim access token for canary A.

—Markus
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@biocrest.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP update — procurement window slipping

Emily / team —

Agree with Markus. Operational proposal to keep your evaluation cadence without full contract execution:

1) Canary A (scope + acceptance) — target start 2026-05-25
   - Scope: inference API (models M1/M2), telemetry dashboard access, limited token quota (10k/day)
   - Acceptance test set and runbook to be shared by 5/22
   - Duration: 14 days

2) Canary B (expanded) — gated by signed MPA, but can begin as a shadow test once procurement provides LOI

3) MAP rebaseline proposal (if procurement signs after 6/14):
   - New target signature: 2026-06-17
   - Staged go-live: production routing 2026-07-01 (soft), full acceptance 2026-07-15

We will keep the original milestone map but add a contingency lane for the canaries and acceptance windows. That should limit downstream impacts (engineering cutovers, training slots).

Ben — I need a one-page MPA template and a token provisioning ETA. Grace — can you attach the minimal test-run checklist we use for canaries?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@biocrest.com>
Cc: procure@biocrest.com
Date: 2026-05-19T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP update — procurement window slipping

Emily — looping in procurement to acknowledge the revised timeline and to flag any redlines that will affect the MPA.

Operational notes from my side: legal can turn a one-page MPA within 48 business hours for standard pilot terms (liability cap, data controls mirror SOW). Token provisioning for a scoped canary is ~4 business hours after MPA countersign.

If procurement will only accept a PO + SOW (no MPA), we should know that ASAP — that changes the commercial cadence and might require finance approval for credit holds.

I'll draft the MPA and circulate as a DOCX later today.

—Ben
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@biocrest.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@biocrest.com>, procure@biocrest.com
Date: 2026-05-20T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP update — procurement window slipping

Thanks for the rapid response. To be transparent: procurement's current internal sign-off meeting is now 6/14 and our budget committee only meets quarterly. Unless there's an urgent exec escalation, we cannot guarantee anything earlier.

We like the staggered canary idea. For firm commitments: if Redwood can issue an MPA with scoped usage and a credit hold until final SOW signing, procurement is comfortable moving the LOI through the channel and prioritizing the 6/14 review. One caveat — all pilot-like agreements need to be presented to legal with a one-line summary of risk and credit exposure.

Tom Hayes
VP, Programs — Biocrest Health
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: emily.zhao@biocrest.com, tom.hayes@biocrest.com, procure@biocrest.com
Date: 2026-05-21T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: potential >3-week slip — exec alignment recommended

Team — logging an internal escalation and recommended next steps. If the procurement sign-off remains 6/14, we should expect at minimum a 3-week slip to the official close and a phased go-live. Impact summary:
- Reserved capacity: keep warm for 30 days; cost impact nominal but needs exec approval beyond 45 days.
- Sales/Rev recognition: shift to staged recognition; finance ops should be notified.
- Resources: engineering cutover window needs a 2-week float on top of the new target.

Recommended actions:
1) Exec sync (30m) w/ Ben, Laura, Grace, and one director from Legal & Finance — propose 5/22 11:00 PT
2) Approve MPA template and interim credit approach (Ben to circulate)
3) Share the canary A runbook with Biocrest and provision scoped token on countersign

Attaching an escalation summary for the execs. If approved, I'll send the short invite and include finance/legal points.

—Markus
Attachment: escalation_summary.pdf
